rows: Python is still number 1 at 20.86%, though it fell 2.51 points in a year. Java rose to number 3 at 8.89% and passed C++.
TIOBE measures how popular a language is in searches. It does not measure hiring or quality.
About 58% of developers use Python, up 7 points in a year. 84% use or plan to use AI tools, and 51% of professionals use them daily.
It tells you what developers use, not what freshers get hired for in India.

Python gained about 850,000 contributors, up almost 49%, and Java gained about 175,000, up about 21%. TypeScript passed Python and JavaScript as the most used language by contributor count. India added over 5.2 million developers in 2025.
GitHub counts accounts, not jobs. A growing pool of Indian developers also suggests more people chasing each junior seat.
PrepNPlaced report on LinkedIn and Naukri postings, 26 September to 26 October 2026
Of 18,752 postings, 4.3% were entry level and 51.5% were senior. Python appeared in about 28.2% and SQL in 21.6%. Data engineering rose from 4.3% to 7.7% of postings between July and October.
That report does not give a Java share, so check Java postings yourself.
